Criterion: Verify that the propulsion control integration, control mechanisms, feedback loops, automatic throttle control systems, symmetric and asymmetric thrust controlling conditions, special thrust control conditions, atmospherics, and hypersonic effects on thrust control are safe. Standard: The probability of air vehicle loss due to VCF integration with propulsion does not exceed PLOC. This probability accounts for the interdependence of all air vehicle functions affecting the propulsion function. The VCF compensates for any hazardous flight condition which results from asymmetric propulsion system. The propulsion control functions integrated with the VCF provide: a. Fault tolerance. b. Redundancy management. c. Integrated diagnostics and reporting/annunciation. d. Data latency and equivalent time delay requirements. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, simulation, and review of documentation. The quantitative flight safety requirements including asymmetric operation is verified by the FMECA. Integrated propulsion control requirements are verified by analysis, simulation, SIL, FMETand ground tests. References: JSSG-2008: 3.0, 3.1, 3.1.2, 3.1.5.3, 3.1.5.5, 3.1.7.3, 3.1.11, 3.1.13, 3.1.13.3, 3.1.17, 3.2.2.2.9, 3.2.2.5.1.1, 3.2.2.5.4.5, 3.3.1, associated section 4 paragraphs. 14 CFR 25.901.

Standard: Where the propulsion system is used for control in the pitch, roll, yaw, or heave axis: a. Single failures in the propulsion system and nominal operation under expected worst-case engine performance do not degrade the VCF below Operational State II. b. Propulsion system failures more probable than PLOC divided by ten do not the degrade VCF below Operational State IV. Failures resulting in asymmetric thrust do not degrade the VCF below Operational State III. Propulsion system health monitoring is provided to the VCF. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review of the interface and performance requirements between VCF and propulsion. Analysis.
  (1) Verify FMECA and SSHA are completed to identify failures, failure rates, and consequences of propulsion system failures.
  (2) Identify worst-case engine performance under expected environmental conditions with consideration to end of life performance.
  (3) Analyze VCF impact due to identified worst-case engine performance. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct FMET to examine the propulsion system integration.
    (2) Lab test: Conduct test in a flight crew evaluation facility, a handling qualities simulation facility, or SIL to verify the VCF performance does not degrade below Operational State II for either worst-case engine performance or single failures of the propulsion system (or below Operational State III for failures resulting in asymmetric thrust). Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
      (1) Conduct flight operations evaluating integration with propulsion across the envelope during normal operation. Test.
    (3) Flight test: Conduct flight test operations evaluating the performance of the propulsion system across the envelope during normal operation.
